{{Short description|Strange attractor connected by two 2-dimensional rings}}
[[Image:DoubleScrollAttractor3D.svg|thumb|300px|A double-scroll Chen attractor from a simulation]]

In the mathematics of [[dynamical system]]s, the '''double-scroll attractor''' (sometimes known as '''Chua's attractor''') is a [[strange attractor]] observed from a physical electronic [[Chaos theory|chaotic]] circuit (generally, [[Chua's circuit]]) with a single [[Nonlinear system|nonlinear]] resistor (see [[Chua's diode]]). The double-scroll system is often described by a system of three nonlinear ordinary differential equations and a 3-segment piecewise-linear equation (see [[Chua's circuit|Chua's equations]]). This makes the system easily simulated numerically and easily manifested physically due to Chua's circuits' simple design.

Using a Chua's circuit, this shape is viewed on an oscilloscope using the X, Y, and Z output signals of the circuit. This chaotic attractor is known as the double scroll because of its shape in three-dimensional space, which is similar to two saturn-like rings connected by swirling lines.

The attractor was first observed in simulations, then realized physically after [[Leon Chua]] invented the [[Autonomous circuit|autonomous]] chaotic circuit which became known as Chua's circuit.<ref>{{cite journal | last = Matsumoto | first = Takashi | title = A Chaotic Attractor from Chua's Circuit  | journal = IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems | volume = CAS-31 | issue = 12 | pages = 1055–1058 | publisher = [[IEEE]] | date = December 1984 | doi = 10.1109/TCS.1984.1085459 | url = http://www.eecs.berkeley.edu/~chua/papers/Matsumoto84.pdf}}</ref> The double-scroll attractor from the Chua circuit was rigorously proven to be chaotic<ref>{{cite journal|last=Chua|first=Leon |author2=Motomasa Komoru |author3=Takashi Matsumoto|title=The Double-Scroll Family|journal=IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems|date=November 1986|volume=CAS-33|issue=11|url=http://www.eecs.berkeley.edu/~chua/papers/Chua86.pdf}}</ref> through a number of [[Poincaré map|Poincaré return maps]] of the attractor explicitly derived by way of compositions of the [[eigenvector]]s of the 3-dimensional state space.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Chua|first=Leon|year=2007|title=Chua circuits|journal=Scholarpedia|volume=2|issue=10|page=1488|doi=10.4249/scholarpedia.1488 |bibcode=2007SchpJ...2.1488C|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Numerical analysis of the double-scroll attractor has shown that its geometrical structure is made up of an infinite number of fractal-like layers. Each cross section appears to be a [[fractal]] at all scales.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Chua|first=Leon|year=2007|title=Fractal Geometry of the Double-Scroll Attractor|journal=Scholarpedia|volume=2|issue=10|page=1488|doi=10.4249/scholarpedia.1488 |bibcode=2007SchpJ...2.1488C|doi-access=free}}</ref> Recently, there has also been reported the discovery of [[Hidden oscillation|hidden attractors]] within the double scroll.<ref name=2011-PLA-Hidden-Chua-attractor>{{cite journal |author1=Leonov G.A. |author2=Vagaitsev V.I. |author3=Kuznetsov N.V. | year = 2011 | title = Localization of hidden Chua's attractors | journal = Physics Letters A | volume = 375 | issue = 23 |
url = http://www.math.spbu.ru/user/nk/PDF/2011-PhysLetA-Hidden-Attractor-Chua.pdf |
pages = 2230&ndash;2233 | doi = 10.1016/j.physleta.2011.04.037|bibcode=2011PhLA..375.2230L }}</ref>

In 1999 [[Chen Guanrong|Guanrong Chen]] (陈关荣) and Ueta proposed another double scroll chaotic attractor, called the Chen system or Chen attractor.<ref>Chen G., Ueta T. Yet another chaotic attractor. Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos, 1999 9:1465.</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=CHEN|first1=GUANRONG|last2=UETA|first2=TETSUSHI|title=Yet Another Chaotic Attractor|date=July 1999|journal=International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos|volume=09|issue=7|pages=1465–1466|doi=10.1142/s0218127499001024|bibcode=1999IJBC....9.1465C |issn=0218-1274}}</ref>

== Chen attractor ==
The Chen system is defined as follows<ref name=":1" />

<math>\frac{dx(t)}{dt}=a(y(t)-x(t))</math>

<math>\frac{dy(t)}{dt}=(c-a)x(t)-x(t)z(t)+cy(t)</math>

<math>\frac{dz(t)}{dt}=x(t)y(t)-bz(t)</math>

Plots of Chen attractor can be obtained with the [[Runge-Kutta method]]:<ref>阎振亚著 《复杂非线性波的构造性理论及其应用》第17页 SCIENCEP 2007年</ref>

parameters: a = 40, c = 28, b = 3

initial conditions: x(0) = -0.1, y(0) = 0.5, z(0) = -0.6

==Other attractors==
Multiscroll attractors also called ''n''-scroll attractor include the Lu Chen attractor, the modified Chen chaotic attractor, PWL Duffing attractor, [[Rabinovich-Fabrikant equation|Rabinovich Fabrikant attractor]], modified Chua chaotic attractor, that is, multiple scrolls in a single attractor.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal|last=Chen|first=Guanrong|author2=Jinhu Lu|title=Generating Multiscroll Chaotic Attractors: Theories, Methods and Applications|journal=International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos|year=2006|volume=16|issue=4|pages=775&ndash;858|url = http://www.ee.cityu.edu.hk/~gchen/pdf/LC-IJBC06-survey.pdf|access-date=2012-02-16|doi=10.1142/s0218127406015179|bibcode=2006IJBC...16..775L}}</ref>

===Lu Chen attractor===
[[Image:LuChenAttractor3D.svg|thumb|Lu Chen Attractor]]
An extended Chen system with multiscroll was proposed by Jinhu Lu (吕金虎) and Guanrong Chen<ref name=":0" />

Lu Chen system equation

<math>\frac{dx(t)}{dt}=a(y(t)-x(t))</math>

<math>\frac{dy(t)}{dt}=x(t)-x(t)z(t)+cy(t)+u</math>

<math>\frac{dz(t)}{dt}=x(t)y(t)-bz(t)</math>

parameters：a = 36, c = 20, b = 3, u = -15.15

initial conditions：x(0) = .1, y(0) = .3, z(0) = -.6

===Modified Lu Chen attractor===
[[Image:LuChenAttractorModified3D.svg|thumb|Lu Chen Attractor modified]]
System equations:<ref name=":0" />

<math>\frac{dx(t)}{dt}=a(y(t)-x(t)), </math>

<math>\frac{dy(t)}{dt}=(c-a)x(t)-x(t)f+cy(t), </math>

<math>\frac{dz(t)}{dt}=x(t)y(t)-bz(t)</math>

In which

<math> f = d0z(t) + d1z(t -  \tau ) - d2\sin(z(t - \tau ))</math>

params := a = 35, c = 28, b = 3, d0 = 1, d1 = 1, d2 = -20..20, tau = .2

initv := x(0) = 1, y(0) = 1, z(0) = 14

===Modified Chua chaotic attractor===
[[Image:ChuaAttractorModified.svg|thumb|Chua Attractor]]
In 2001, Tang et al. proposed a modified Chua chaotic system<ref>{{cite journal|last=Chen|first=Guanrong|author2=Jinhu Lu|title=Generating Multiscroll Chaotic Attractors: Theories, Methods and Applications|journal=International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos|year=2006|volume=16|issue=4|pages=793–794|url = http://www.ee.cityu.edu.hk/~gchen/pdf/LC-IJBC06-survey.pdf|access-date=2012-02-16|doi=10.1142/s0218127406015179|bibcode=2006IJBC...16..775L}}</ref>

<math>\frac{dx(t)}{dt}= \alpha (y(t)-h)</math>

<math>\frac{dy(t)}{dt}=x(t)-y(t)+z(t)</math>

<math>\frac{dz(t)}{dt}=-\beta y(t)</math>

In which

<math>h := -b \sin\left(\frac{\pi x(t)}{2a}+d\right)</math>

params := alpha = 10.82, beta = 14.286, a = 1.3, b = .11, c = 7, d = 0

initv := x(0) = 1, y(0) = 1, z(0) = 0

===PWL Duffing chaotic attractor===
[[Image:PWLDuffingAttractor.svg|thumb|PWL Duffing Attractor]]
Aziz Alaoui investigated PWL Duffing equation in 2000:<ref>J. Lu, G. Chen p. 837</ref>

PWL Duffing system:

<math>\frac{dx(t)}{dt}=y(t)</math>

<math>\frac{dy(t)}{dt}=-m_1x(t)-(1/2(m_0-m_1))(|x(t)+1|-|x(t)-1|)-ey(t)+\gamma \cos(\omega t)</math>

params := e = .25, gamma = .14+(1/20)i, m0 = -0.845e-1, m1 = .66, omega = 1; c := (.14+(1/20)i)，i=-25...25;

initv := x(0) = 0, y(0) = 0;

===Modified Lorenz chaotic system===
[[File:LorenzModified3D.svg|thumb|Lorenz system modified]]
Miranda & Stone proposed a modified Lorenz system:<ref>J.Liu and G Chen p834</ref>

<math>\frac{dx(t)}{dt} = 1/3*(-(a+1)x(t)+a-c+z(t)y(t))+((1-a)(x(t)^2-y(t)^2)+(2(a+c-z(t)))x(t)y(t))</math><math>\frac{1}{3\sqrt{x(t)^2+y(t)^2}}</math>

<math>\frac{dy(t)}{dt}= 1/3((c-a-z(t))x(t)-(a+1)y(t))+((2(a-1))x(t)y(t)+(a+c-z(t))(x(t)^2-y(t)^2))</math><math>\frac{1}{3\sqrt{x(t)^2+y(t)^2}}</math>

<math>\frac{dz(t)}{dt} = 1/2(3x(t)^2y(t)-y(t)^3)-bz(t)</math>

parameters： a = 10, b = 8/3, c = 137/5;

initial conditions： x(0) = -8, y(0) = 4, z(0) = 10
